The problem · Why it matters

Word of mouth has a ceiling. Google does not.

Your best work already speaks for itself. The trouble is the customer who has never met you, deciding between you and the next bloke right now, on their phone.

They check you before they call

Nobody rings a builder cold any more. They look you up first. No site, or one that looks like 2013, and you have lost the job before you ever knew it existed.

Tidy beats good

The builder who looks more professional online wins work off better builders every single day. It is not fair and it does not care how good your work is.

Referrals leak

Someone recommends you. They go searching, they cannot find you, they ring whoever turns up first. That is your reputation paying someone else's mortgage.

The case for it · Why a website at all

Everything you do to win work ends up here.

Someone searches your name. Someone scrolls past you on Instagram. Someone gets handed your number at a barbecue. Someone taps an ad. All four end in the same place, on your website, working out whether you are worth ringing.

Word of mouth is the best lead you will ever get, and it is the one you have the least control over. It stops when the talking stops. A website does not stop. It works while you are on site, while you are asleep, and while the bloke down the road is still thinking about ringing someone.

That is why it is the backbone and not the extra. The posting, the ads, the referrals, the signage on the ute, all of it points at one place. If that place is weak, everything pointing at it is wasted.

The process · Mostly my job, not yours

You stay on the tools.

Four steps. You see something real before you pay a cent, and the only work on your side is sending photos.

  1. 01 Day 0

    A quick chat

    Fifteen minutes. You tell me what the business does and which jobs you want more of. No deck, no pitch, no obligation.

  2. 02 48 hours

    I build you a demo, free

    Not a mockup, a working site with your name on it that you can click through on your phone. You have not paid me anything at this point and you are not committed to anything.

  3. 03 2 to 3 weeks

    You send photos, I build it properly

    A handful of good shots off your phone and the basics. That is your whole job. I write the wording, build every page, and you review it and tell me what to change.

  4. 04 Ongoing

    It goes live and I keep it running

    I host it, keep it secure and patched, and it starts getting found. Hosting and security is $90 a month from the day it goes live.

Questions · Answered straight

Before you get in touch.

How long does it take?

Two to three weeks from the day I have your photos and the basics. You see a free demo before that, usually within 48 hours, so you know what you are getting before you commit to anything.

What do I actually have to do?

Send me a handful of good photos of your work, tell me your services and the areas you cover, and look over the draft. That is the whole job. I write the wording, build it, set it up and host it.

What does it cost?

The standard build is $4,000. Half to start, half when you are happy with it. After it goes live, hosting and security is $90 a month. Bigger scope, more pages, migrations and custom work get quoted properly after a look.

Will people actually find it on Google?

The site is built to rank from day one: your services and areas each get their own page, the technical setup is done properly, and the schema tells Google exactly what you do and where. Nobody honest can promise you a position, because Google decides that. What I can promise is that the groundwork is done right, and on the Growth plan I keep working on it every month.

Who owns the website?

You do. Your domain, your content, your site. No lock-in, and if you ever want to take it somewhere else you can.

What if I need something changed later?

On the Growth plan every edit you need is handled, no hourly billing and no waiting. On hosting only, small text fixes are included and anything bigger gets quoted before I start.

Why should I trust you with this?

I laid pipe, worked a coal port and did marketing for a real estate company before this. I know what a quote costs you to write and what a dead lead feels like. And you do not have to trust me up front: I build you a free demo of your own site first, and you decide from there.
